newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian share trade down, market seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Latvian share trade down, market seen stable.

text.p: Latvian shares closed slightly lower on Friday ahead of the weekend amid lower turnover with dealers looking forward to a pickup only in the autumn.
Turnover slipped to 57,000 lats from 66,000 lats and the Rietumu Bank index was down 1.66 points to 152.68. The bourse index fell 7.42 points or 1.87 percent to 388.64.
Unibanka was most traded on 13,600 lats, down four santimes to 3.35 lats.
Dealers said the first-half reporting season brought results in line with or better than expectations but did not see a pickup in trade until the end of the summer holiday period.
"I hope that the expected autumn revival will coincide with extended trading hours on the Riga bourse," said Karlis Krastinsh, head of the securities department of Saules Bank.
The market currently has a price-fixing session in the morning, after which bids and offers at a set price can be made.
The bourse hopes to introduce continuous trade for some stocks towards the end of the year.
Valmiera Glassfibre was also active, turning over 10,700 lats and adding one santime to 1.37.
Riga Transport Fleet, which climbed on Thursday after its first-half result, slipped back to 1.30 lats from 1.43 on trade of 6,400 lats.
The firm had a first-half net profit of 1.8 million lats.
"The price could be higher, but investors are slightly on their guard due to a certain lack of transparency," said Leonid Ruderman, dealer with Parex Bank.
"But in general Fleet is a profitable company," he added.
Daugavpils Chain was also amongst the most active on turnover of 6,500 lats but was unchanged at 1.70 lats.
